sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. New research on Tivoid and its place within Bantoid. Slides, Bantu VI, University of Helsinki, 22 June 2016. 27 slides.
sources.note: Slides on Tivoid vowels, consonants and verb-stem tonal alternation (Tiv/Iceve examples). Abɔ̃ appears only in the background/classification tables. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. The Tivoid languages: classification and comparative wordlist. Circulation draft, 15 September 2016 (Bantu VI, Helsinki). Cambridge: KWEF. 20 pp. (= Glottolog ref 78922 'The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List')
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Phonology and morphology' (printed p. 3 = p. 5) is family-level only: 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only five languages, Tiv, Iyive, Iceve, Esimbi and Ugarə.' 3.3 Tones: 'Tiv and Ugarə are two-tone languages, with low tones causing automatic downstep.. Esimbi has three tones as well as rising and falling glide tones.' No statement on Abon phonology; the word 'stress' does not occur. Abon data source = 'Koops ms., IL survey' (Table 1, p. 2). Same file served at the 2025-11-13 Internet Archive copy, so this is the current version.

sources.citation: Anonymous, n.d. 'Abon Language, Etymology, History, Grammar, Phonology, Morphology'. Web page at internationalphoneticalphabet.org/abon/ (no author, no date, no references). Together with its twin 'The Abon Language' at glocal.soas.ac.uk/abon/ (The GLOCAL site; likewise unauthored, undated, unreferenced).
sources.note: The page asserts, without data or citation: 'Abon typically employs a system of high, mid, and low tones, which must be learned and applied accurately by speakers.' and 'Each syllable in Abon can carry one of these tones, and tonal distinctions can change the meaning of words entirely.' The glocal.soas.ac.uk twin says 'The Abon language has a relatively simple phonology, with only seven vowel sounds and a limited number of consonants' and mentions 'the use of tone to distinguish between different meanings of words.'
